capabilities.title: Grid search enumerates the full cartesian product of a discrete configuration space
capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through their public optimize entry point with algorithm "grid": Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_grid.py (Traigent develop bf57c2b5) and the JS SDK parity conformance test (develop cb4fa5de). Both assert raw invocation count, no duplicates, set equality, and max-trials truncation. Parameter ordering is not part of the contract.

capabilities.title: Multi-objective min-max normalization, sum-to-one weighting, zero-span fallback and dominance guard
capabilities.rationale: Both SDKs pass this fixture through public APIs: Python SDK tests/unit/parity/test_conformance_multi_objective.py (Traigent develop f7f0f47d) via ObjectiveSchema.from_objectives, OptimizationResult.score_trials and traigent.optimize; JS SDK parity conformance test (develop 25e4a855) via the public scoreTrials export and optimize. Both assert normalized weights, per-trial normalized and weighted scores within 1e-9, the unique-max best trial, and the 0.99 dominance guard.

capabilities.title: Stop limits: maximum trials, cumulative cost cap and maximum total examples

entryPoints: @traigent/sdk optimize({ budget: { maxCostUsd }, execution: { maxTotalExamples } }) with maxTrials

capabilities.rationale: The fixture states the stop rules directly: a trial limit, a cost cap where the crossing trial finishes and counts, and an example cap that truncates the last trial. Invalid limit values and negative trial costs are asserted only as rejections. Plateau stopping, cost estimation, a default cost cap, failed-trial handling, a grid exhausted exactly at a limit and precedence between simultaneous limits are open product decisions and deliberately out of scope. Conformance adapters for both SDKs are pending.
capabilities.targetMilestone: SDKS-3: Python and JS conformance adapters
